title: Johnson–Lindenstrauss concentration for a single vector
statement:
Let $k \ge 1$, and let $A$ be a random $k \times d$ real matrix on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ whose $kd$ entries $A_{ij}$ are jointly independent, each Gaussian with law $N(0, 1/k)$. Then for every fixed vector $x \in \bbr^d$ and every $\varepsilon$ with $0 < \varepsilon < 1$,
\[
  \mu\bigl\{\,\omega : \bigl|\,\|A(\omega)\,x\|^2 - \|x\|^2\,\bigr| > \varepsilon\,\|x\|^2 \,\bigr\}
  \;\le\; 2\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{k\,\varepsilon^2}{8}\Bigr),
\]
where $\|A(\omega)\,x\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm of the image $A(\omega)\,x \in \bbr^k$.
hypotheses_covered: A is (measurably) a random k×d matrix
each entry A_ij is distributed as N(0, 1/k)
the entries are jointly independent (row entries independent and rows independent)
x is a fixed vector in ℝ^d
replaced:
Let $A:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^{k\times d}$ be a random matrix under a probability
measure $\mu$ whose entries $A_{ij}$ are each $N(0,1/k)$ and are jointly
independent (row entries and row vectors alike).  For any fixed
$x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$,
\[
  \mu\bigl\{\omega \mid \texttt{BadSingle}\,\varepsilon\,(A\,\omega)\,x\bigr\}
  \;\le\; 2\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{k\,\varepsilon^2}{8}\Bigr).
\]
The proof handles $x=0$ via \texttt{concentration\_zero} and the general case by
showing each row projection $\sum_j A_{ij}\,x_j$ is Gaussian with variance
$\|x\|^2/k$, establishing independence of row projections via
\texttt{rows\_indep}, and then applying \texttt{chi\_squared\_tail}.
